rows.rewrite: net billing cost responsibility meter interconnection distributed generation facility
rows.answer:
The Distributed Generator must pay for all costs of the interconnection facilities up to the interconnection point, including the installation of meters [S3][S5]. This rule is from the repealed Net Metering Regulations 2015, but it still applies to existing licences and agreements under the savings clause of the Prosumer Regulations 2026 [S6].

[S3] Net Metering Regs 2015, reg. 12(1), p. 7 (repealed)
[S5] Net Metering Regs 2015, reg. 12(3), p. 7 (repealed)
[S6] Prosumer Regs 2026, reg. 21(2), p. 7

drafts.text: The Distributed Generator must pay for all costs of the interconnection facilities up to the interconnection point, including the installation of meters. This is the rule from the repealed Net Metering Regulations, but it still applies to existing licences and agreements under the savings clause of the Prosumer Regulations 2026. [S3][S6]

The Distributed Generator must pay for all costs of the interconnection facilities up to the interconnection point, including the installation of meters [S3][S5]. This rule is from the repealed Net Metering Regulations 2015, but it still applies to existing licences and agreements under the savings clause of the Prosumer Regulations 2026 [S6].

rows.rewrite: bidirectional meter requirement for distributed generation facility net billing prosumer detection bill
rows.answer:
A solar (distributed generation) connection must use either a standard meter that can register electricity flow in two directions, or two separate meters—one for electricity sold to the licensee and one for electricity purchased from the licensee [S2]. The repealed Net Metering Regulations also required equipment to measure flow in both directions, but that rule is no longer in force except where the savings clause applies [S5][S6].

[S2] Prosumer Regs 2026, reg. 5(1), p. 4
[S5] Net Metering Regs 2015, reg. 13(1), p. 7 (repealed)
[S6] Prosumer Regs 2026, reg. 21(2), p. 7

drafts.text:
A meter for a solar (distributed generation) connection must be able to record electricity flowing in both directions. The licensee may require either a single standard meter that registers two‑way flow, or two separate meters—one for electricity sold to the licensee and one for electricity purchased from the licensee [S2]. 

The earlier Net Metering Regulations also required equipment to measure flow in both directions, but those rules have been repealed; they only continue to apply to existing agreements under the savings clause (Prosumer Regs 2026, reg. 21(2)) [S5][S6].

A solar (distributed generation) connection must use either a standard meter that can register electricity flow in two directions, or two separate meters—one for electricity sold to the licensee and one for electricity purchased from the licensee [S2]. The repealed Net Metering Regulations also required equipment to measure flow in both directions, but that rule is no longer in force except where the savings clause applies [S5][S6].

rows.rewrite: old net metering export tariff fuel adjustment taxes included
rows.answer:
The DISCO paid only the off‑peak rate for exported units under the old net‑metering rules [S1].  Fuel‑price adjustment, duties and other taxes were not payable by the DISCO [S1].  This rule is from the repealed Net Metering Regulations 2015 and still applies to existing agreements as specified in the savings clause of the Prosumer Regulations 2026 [S6].

[S1] Net Metering Regs 2015, reg. 14(4), p. 7 (repealed)
[S6] Prosumer Regs 2026, reg. 21(2), p. 7

rows.rewrite: avoid late payment surcharge billing cycle payment deadline DISCO
rows.answer:
Pay your bill on or before the due date [S1]. If you use a cheque, pay‑order or bank draft, deposit it at the Revenue Office and the bank at least three days before the due date so it clears in time [S1]. You may also avoid the surcharge by obtaining an extension of the due date, because a surcharge is not imposed when the due date is extended [S2].

rows.rewrite: late meter reading extended billing cycle unit charge calculation detection bill
rows.answer:
When the billing cycle exceeds the normal month, DISCO must apply pro‑rata billing to calculate the units for that period [S1]. The actual units recorded are divided by the number of days taken and then multiplied by the standard 30‑day month to obtain the chargeable units [S1]. If the resulting chargeable units are within the Life Line limit (up to 50 units), they are billed at the Life Line rate for the current month and any excess is carried forward to the next billing cycle [S1].

[S1] Consumer Service Manual 2025, clause 6.1.1.1, p. 45

drafts.text: When a billing cycle runs longer than the normal month, the units are calculated on a pro‑rata basis. The actual units read are divided by the number of days taken and then multiplied by the standard 30‑day month (e.g., 54 units in 33 days → 54 ÷ 33 × 30 = 49 units) [S1]. For Lifeline consumers, the first 49 units are charged at the Lifeline rate for that month and any units above the Lifeline threshold are carried forward to the next billing cycle [S1].

When the billing cycle exceeds the normal month, DISCO must apply pro‑rata billing to calculate the units for that period [S1]. The actual units recorded are divided by the number of days taken and then multiplied by the standard 30‑day month to obtain the chargeable units [S1]. If the resulting chargeable units are within the Life Line limit (up to 50 units), they are billed at the Life Line rate for the current month and any excess is carried forward to the next billing cycle [S1].

rows.rewrite: exceeding sanctioned load actions by DISCO load increase penalty billing cycle
rows.answer:
If you use load above your sanctioned amount, the DISCO will first issue a notice asking you to apply for an extension of load within 15 days [S2]. If you do not apply for the extension and complete the required formalities, the DISCO may disconnect your supply [S2][S4]. Additionally, the DISCO may immediately change your tariff to a higher category (for example, from B‑1 to B‑2) and recover the difference in charges for the period of misuse, but the retrospective recovery cannot exceed six months [S1].

[S2] Consumer Service Manual 2025, clause 8.2.10, p. 55
[S4] Consumer Service Manual 2025, clause 8.1, p. 54
[S1] Consumer Service Manual 2025, clause 7.5.2, p. 52
